questions.q: A single Salesforce org serves three business units. What is the recommended default for concepts like Account and Opportunity that genuinely mean the same thing across all three units?
options: A separate custom object per business unit, even for shared concepts
Three separate Salesforce orgs, one per business unit
A shared core of standard objects used consistently across all business units
No object at all — track everything in spreadsheets outside Salesforce
questions.explain: When a concept like 'the customer' or 'the deal' genuinely means the same thing across business units, it belongs on a shared core object rather than being forked per unit.

questions.q: What does a record type let a single object do across different business units?
options: Store data in a physically separate database table per business unit
Carry different page layouts, picklist values, and required fields per business unit while the underlying schema stays unified
Automatically translate field values between business units
Bypass Salesforce's sharing model entirely
questions.explain: Record types let one object present differently per business unit (layouts, picklists, required fields) without forking the schema, so every report still queries across a single, unified object.

questions.q: A manufacturing business unit tracks warranty claims that no other business unit has any analog for. Where should this detail live?
options: As generic fields bolted onto the shared Account object that only make sense for one unit
Nowhere — it should not be tracked in Salesforce at all
As a record type on the Contact object
In its own business-unit-specific custom object, related back to the shared Account or Opportunity
questions.explain: Detail with no analog in other business units belongs in its own custom object related back to the shared core, rather than forced into generic fields on a shared object that only serve one unit.

questions.q: How should visibility between business units' records on the same shared object typically be controlled?
options: By exporting each unit's data into a separate spreadsheet
Through Salesforce's sharing model (role hierarchy, sharing rules), keyed off a Business Unit field or owning role
By creating a separate Salesforce org for each business unit's records
Visibility cannot be controlled at the record level in Salesforce
questions.explain: Record-level separation via sharing rules, role hierarchy, and a Business Unit field is how a single shared schema still supports per-business-unit visibility control, without needing a separate org or schema.

questions.q: What is the signal that two business units may no longer belong on the same shared object model?
options: They both use the Account object
They are both served by the same Salesforce org
Their definitions of an object have diverged so far that reconciling them needs an unmanageable thicket of conditional layouts and validation rules
They both have more than 1,000 records
questions.explain: When record types, a Business Unit field, and extension objects can no longer reasonably reconcile two business units' divergent definitions of the same object, that's the signal to isolate that object or reopen the single-org-vs-multi-org question.
